$comment: Committed expected failure counts for the Slice-0 thesis invariants.
These numbers are MEASURED, never predicted. Each check exits 0 iff its finding
count equals the number here — a count that DROPS is red too, which forces the
decrement into the same PR as the fix and makes a silent regression impossible
in either direction. A baseline decremented without an accompanying source
change is visible in review as a one-line diff with no fix beside it.
Every entry is currently NON-ZERO on purpose. An invariant that passes on day
one is measuring nothing. When a `blockedBy` slice lands, that slice decrements
its own baseline; when a baseline reaches 0 the `--expect` gate is removed and
the check switches to zero-tolerance (spec Phase 4).
Measured 2026-07-19 on ci/thesis-invariants against a freshly built compiler

governed.reason: Scorecard §Governed 4/4 — CLEARED 2026-07-19 by GO1 + GO2 in one commit (2→0), the ratchet's first entry to reach zero. Was 2: (1) 'Rate limiting fails closed — ❌ — agent-service.ts:215 — `if (rateLimitSpec !== null && rateLimitPlugin)`. Declare `$rate-limit`, omit the plugin, get silently unlimited' (probe G1). GO1 split the guard so an absent plugin returns 429 RATE_LIMIT_MISSING, mirroring the `$scope`/401 AUTH_MISSING posture. (2) 'Bridge handshake verified — ❌ — BRIDGE_PROTOCOL_VERSION is sent (bridge-client.ts:67) and exported (index.ts:15) — and never checked server-side' (probe G2, one finding covering all three sub-probes: one defect, the absent comparison). GO2 wrote the comparison: `callTool` refuses to delegate to a channel that has not completed a valid `hello` (503 BRIDGE_UNVERIFIED), and an unverified channel may send no frame other than `hello`. The no-bridge headless/CI path (agent-server.ts:279) is untouched and requires no handshake. Both slices landed with bidirectional named tests — a declared control with its plugin absent DENIES, an undeclared control still DISPATCHES — and the probe's self-test was re-based in the same commit from shim-simulated fixes to real-code regressions plus a must-delegate positive control, so it still discriminates rather than going vacuous at zero.
governed.ratchet: CLEARED. GO1 + GO2 landed together and took 2→0. Per spec Phase 4, this entry is now eligible to drop its `--expect` gate and switch to zero-tolerance.

dual-audience.reason: Scorecard §Dual-audience 2/4 — the two remaining ❌ rows are both in packages/plugin-agent-readiness/src/content-negotiation.ts. (DA-a) 'A markdown representation can be produced — ❌ — MarkdownResolver has zero production implementations. Every reference is the interface declaration (content-negotiation.ts:13), the config field (:22), or a test mock'. (DA-b) 'Negotiation reaches non-Accept clients — ❌ — no user-agent handling in content-negotiation.ts — Accept-header only, and AI crawlers don't send it' (2/3 cells wrong: GPTBot and ClaudeBot, neither sending an Accept header). DA-c and DA-d are CLEARED — see expectChangedReason.
dual-audience.expectChangedReason: CLEARED BY FIX (2026-07-20), 4→2, both defects repaired in the commit that carries this decrement. (DA-c) packages/router/src/server.ts now calls renderToString(component, { hydratable: true }); (DA-d) packages/app/src/prerender.ts does the same at both the layout-shell render and the page render. Every data-aihu-path marker in ssr.ts is gated on `opts?.hydratable ?? false`, so the missing options object was the whole defect at each site. These two decrements are counted separately, as baselines.json required: the router edit and the SSG-writer edit are independent, and either alone would have moved this by exactly 1. PREREQUISITE: CO5 landed first (commit ec6aee60) — before it, emitting markers would not have helped, because @aihu/server seeded its path walk with '0' while @aihu/arbor's hydrate() hardcoded 'hydrate.0', so no marker could ever be matched. SELF-TEST RE-BASED IN THE SAME COMMIT, following the GO1/GO2 precedent: DA-c's and DA-d's should-flag arms USED to drive the live production path, so repairing production would have made the self-test exit 1 before the real scan and the check would have read as broken rather than as passing. Both positive controls are now simulated regressions — the identical component through the identical renderer with `{ hydratable: false }`, i.e. exactly the edit that would reintroduce the defect — while the live path became the should-not-flag control. The probes still assert marker PRESENCE and text REACHABILITY, never an exact markup blob. Verified after the change: 8 self-test cases pass in both directions, 196 public-entry sources scanned, 2 findings (DA-a, DA-b).

expectHistory.why: FOUNDER SCOPE DECISION — not a regression and not a new defect. Prerender was ruled IN SCOPE, so the check gained the DA-d probe and measured 4 where it measured 3. Nothing was fixed and nothing broke: packages/app/src/prerender.ts:283/:382 had always called renderToString(...) with no options; the check simply had not looked at the SSG path, so a shipping defect went unmeasured.
DA3 + DA3b landed together: hydratable options threaded into the router SSR handler and both SSG writer call sites, on top of CO5's path-key unification.

dual-audience.ratchet: DA1 (MarkdownResolver implementation) takes 2→1; DA2 (UA-aware negotiation) takes 1→0. DA3 (router) and DA3b (SSG writer) are DONE.
